corrected_met.rmr_unit_conversion: RMR_mlkgmin = (RMR_kcal_day / 1440) / 5 / weight_kg * 1000   [kcal/day -> kcal/min -> L O2/min (5 kcal per L) -> mL/kg/min]
corrected_met.units: standard_MET dimensionless (multiples of 3.5 mL O2/kg/min); RMR_mlkgmin in mL O2/kg/min; height cm, weight kg, age years
corrected_met.locator: pacompendium.com/corrected-mets, 'Figure 1' section and the Harris-Benedict / conversion lines under it
corrected_met.evidence: The page divides the standard 3.5 mL/kg/min by a Harris-Benedict predicted RMR (age, height, mass, sex) to get a 'corrected MET', citing Kozey 2010 and Byrne 2005. It says corrected METs may suit individual estimates by clinicians/fitness professionals but should not replace standard METs for population/survey use, and that neither removes all error.
corrected_met.interpretation_note: The page does not state how to turn a corrected MET into kcal. Algebra check (not from the source): if you compute kcal/min = corrected_MET * RMR_mlkgmin * kg * 5 / 1000, the RMR terms cancel and you get the standard MET*3.5*kg*5/1000 result. The correction only changes kcal if you multiply corrected MET by a fixed 1 kcal/kg/h, which mixes the individual and standard RMR. Decide deliberately which you want.

protocol.exercise: 8 machine exercises: half squat, 45-deg leg press, leg extension, horizontal bench press, 45-deg incline bench press, lat pulldown, triceps extension (high pulley), biceps curl (Scott bench, EZ bar)
protocol.reps: 4-5 min continuous bouts at 15 reps/min for 12-24% 1RM; 80% bout to exhaustion

measured.method: Breath-by-breath VO2 (Cosmed K4b2); anaerobic share by accumulated O2 deficit; 1 mL O2 = 5 cal

measured_studies.key_findings: Energy cost rose linearly with %1RM in every exercise; lowest in biceps curl, highest in half squat. At 80% 1RM leg exercises exceeded 20 kcal/min and upper-body exercises were less anaerobic than lower-body.
measured_studies.locator: Abstract; Discussion paragraph 2 (24% 1RM values); Results (range 3.87-11.70). Per-exercise loads are in Table 1 (image, not read).

measured_studies.citation: Mazzetti et al. 2011, Int J Exerc Sci 4(4):273-282

protocol.exercise: maximally explosive squat and bench press

measured.method: Expired-gas indirect calorimetry during and 60 min after; blood lactate

measured_studies.key_findings: Rates were higher with lighter loads and with matched kg per set, but total kcal did not differ among protocols. 60% 1RM rates not in the abstract.
measured_studies.locator: Abstract (sets and reps per protocol are in the full text, not read)

protocol.exercise: bench press, single set to failure

measured.method: Exercise VO2 + blood lactate (anaerobic) + recovery VO2; work measured as weight x displacement

measured_studies.key_findings: Total cost tracked mechanical work (r = 0.87). For strength lifts, anaerobic and recovery components each exceeded aerobic exercise cost.

protocol.exercise: Smith machine incline bench press, squat, deadlift, shoulder shrug, calf raise

measured.method: Exercise O2 + anaerobic estimate + EPOC; work = bar vertical distance x load

measured_studies.key_findings: Cost per set is predictable from mechanical work within each exercise, but the work-to-cost slope differs by exercise. Per-set kJ values are in the full text (not read).
